Germany's Accident Black Spots — where, when and how Germany crashes

Every police-recorded road accident with personal injury in the Destatis Unfallatlas: 2,098,019 accidents across 401 districts (Kreise), 2016–2024 — severity, road users, light and road conditions, black-spot districts per 100,000 inhabitants, and the COVID-19 dip. Geocoded Länder coverage grew year by year and is complete (all 16 Länder) from 2020 — early years are labelled wherever they appear.

Trend — accidents per year (selected severity & road user)

Coverage grew as Länder joined the geocoded atlas: 8 Länder in 2016, 12 in 2017, 13 in 2018, 15 in 2019, all 16 from 2020. Read 2016–2019 growth as coverage growth first, real growth second; the like-for-like era is 2020–2024.

Severity funnel — how many accidents turn deadly?

Each accident is classified by its worst injury (official category UKATEGORIE). The funnel shows the selected slice: all accidents → accidents with serious or fatal injuries → fatal accidents.

Black-spot map — injury accidents per 100,000 inhabitants by district (avg per year, 2020–2024)

Pooled 2020–2024 — the full-coverage era — divided by district population (Destatis Gemeindeverzeichnis, 31 Dec 2024). City districts with heavy through-traffic top the rate ranking; raw counts are led by Berlin and Hamburg. District boundaries: GADM 4.1, simplified; Eisenach is shown inside Wartburgkreis (merged 2021) and Göttingen includes Osterode (merged 2016).

When do accidents happen? — weekday × hour heatmap

Rows Monday–Sunday, columns hour of day (selection above applies). The afternoon rush hour dominates; Friday is the busiest day overall, Tuesday 16:00 is the single busiest cell of the week.

Accidents by hour of day

Peaks at 16:00–17:00. Only 8.0% of accidents happen between 22:00 and 06:00 — but their fatal-accident rate (1.85%) is twice the daytime rate (0.91%).

What kind of accident? — type treemap

Accident type (UTYP1): how the accident came about. Longitudinal-traffic and turning/crossing accidents together are almost half of all injury accidents.

Collision kind (UART) — top patterns

The single most common pattern: a collision with a vehicle that is turning into or crossing the road — 27.2% of all injury accidents.

Who is involved?

An accident can involve several road-user types, so shares add to more than 100%. Bicycles are involved in 29.9% of all injury accidents — and in 32.2% by 2024.

Light conditions

18.9% of accidents happen in darkness, but 26.3% of fatal accidents do — the fatal rate in darkness (1.36%) is well above daylight (0.89%).

Road surface

Three quarters of injury accidents happen on dry roads. Wet roads are not deadlier per accident (fatal rate 0.99% vs 0.99% on dry) — there are simply more dry-road kilometres driven.

Severity split — per 100 accidents (waffle)

Slight injury Serious injury Fatal
Of every 100 injury accidents in the selection: 81 end with slight injuries only, 18 with a serious injury, 1 with a death.

Seasonality — accidents by month

Summer is accident season: June is the peak month, February the quietest. Motorcycle-involved accidents are the most seasonal of all — 51.8% of them fall in June–September.

The COVID dip — monthly accidents 2019 vs 2020 vs 2021

April 2020 recorded 15,603 injury accidents against 21,741 in April 2019 (−28.2%). The full year 2020 fell 11.3% below 2019 (2019 still lacks Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, ≈2% of accidents, so the true dip is slightly smaller).

Which Länder moved? — total accidents 2019 → 2024 (slope)

All 15 Länder covered in 2019 (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern joined in 2020 and is excluded here). Nordrhein-Westfalen remains the largest in absolute terms; most Länder ended 2024 close to their 2019 level.

Highest accident rates — districts per 100k inhabitants

Average per year, pooled 2020–2024, districts with ≥500 accidents in the pool. Small city districts with motorways and through-traffic rank highest.

Most accidents — districts by total (2020–2024)

Berlin alone recorded 60,224 injury accidents in five years — more than the whole of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern in the same period.

Data source

Dataset: Unfallatlas — road accidents with personal injury, one record per accident, geocoded. Published by the Statistischen Ämter des Bundes und der Länder (Destatis / statistical offices of the Länder) via unfallatlas.statistikportal.de; open-data CSV downloads are served from the portal's download host (opengeodata.nrw.de). Licence: dl-de/by-2-0 (Datenlizenz Deutschland — Namensnennung 2.0).
Coverage in this dashboard: reporting years 2016–2024, 2,098,019 verified records (2016: 151,673 · 2017: 195,229 · 2018: 211,868 · 2019: 268,370 · 2020: 237,994 · 2021: 238,826 · 2022: 256,492 · 2023: 269,048 · 2024: 268,519).
Coverage caveat, stated openly: geocoding was rolled out Land by Land — 2016 covers 8 Länder (SH, HH, HB, HE, RP, BW, BY, SN), 2017 adds NI, SL, BB, ST (12), 2018 adds Berlin (13), 2019 adds Nordrhein-Westfalen and Thüringen (15), and only from 2020 are all 16 Länder included. Every published record carries valid coordinates; what grows over time is the set of covered Länder, so pre-2020 totals are not Germany totals.
Severity definition: the atlas classifies each accident by its worst injury (UKATEGORIE): fatal = at least one person killed, serious / slight likewise. It does not publish per-accident counts of injured persons, so this dashboard counts accidents by severity, never invented person counts.
Population: Destatis Gemeindeverzeichnis (municipal register extract, population at 31 Dec 2024), aggregated from municipalities to the 401 districts; Germany total 83,577,140. District boundaries for the map: GADM 4.1 (simplified for the web).
Further caveats: Hamburg and Berlin are coded below district level in the police data (districts / boroughs) and are rolled up to the city district here; for 2016–2017 goods vehicles were recorded under "other vehicle", so the goods-vehicle series starts in 2018.
